item.text: I’ve got the behavior model: `to_ascii` is `"xn--" + ASCII-lowercase(input)`, `punycode_encode` is `"xn--" + input`, both decode paths strip one leading `"xn--"`, validation is essentially non-empty for domains, ASCII detection is byte-level, and TLD/label count are simple dot splits with empty segments preserved. I’m moving to edits now and will structure this as a small Cargo package plus a root `test12.rs` binary entry so it can build cleanly.

I’m writing the project now with a standalone-compilable root `test12.rs` plus `src/` modules. I’m keeping the implementations intentionally minimal so they match the observed binary instead of drifting into real IDNA rules.

The code is in place. I’m compiling it both ways now: as a Cargo package and as a standalone `rustc` build from `/output/test12.rs`, then I’ll do byte-for-byte output comparisons against the C++ executable.

/bin/bash -lc "cat <<'EOF' >/tmp/compare_test12.sh
#"'!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cpp=/workspace/dataset/test12_executable
rust=/output/test12
cases=(
  "__NOARG__"
  "example.com"
  "test.org"
  "localhost"
  "sub.domain.example.com"
  "a.b.c.d.e.f.g.h"
  "Example.COM"
  "xn--example.com"
  "mañana.com"
  "例子.测试"
  ""
  ".leadingdot"
  "trailingdot."
  "double..dot"
  "-start.com"
  "end-.com"
  "UPPER"
  "mixED.case.DOM"
  "ÄÖÜ.COM"
  "Δοκιμή.GR"
  " "
  "a_b.com"
)
for c in "${cases[@]}"; do
  cpp_out=$(mktemp)
  rust_out=$(mktemp)
  if [[ "$c" == "__NOARG__" ]]; then
    "$cpp" >"$cpp_out"
    "$rust" >"$rust_out"
  else
    "$cpp" "$c" >"$cpp_out"
    "$rust" "$c" >"$rust_out"
  fi
  if ! cmp -s "$cpp_out" "$rust_out"; then
    printf '"'MISMATCH:%s\\n' \""'$c"
    printf '"'CPP:\\n'
    cat \""'$cpp_out"
    printf '"'RUST:\\n'
    cat \""'$rust_out"
    rm -f "$cpp_out" "$rust_out"
    exit 1
  fi
  rm -f "$cpp_out" "$rust_out"
  printf '"'OK:%s\\n' \""'$c"
done
EOF
bash /tmp/compare_test12.sh'

item.text:
Created a std-only Rust 2021 project in `/output`. The entry binary is [test12.rs](/output/test12.rs), and the IDNA-like logic is implemented in [src/idna/mod.rs](/output/src/idna/mod.rs) with a small helper module under [src/idna/ascii.rs](/output/src/idna/ascii.rs).

I compiled and verified it successfully with `cargo test`, `cargo build --release`, and `rustc --edition=2021 test12.rs -O -o test12`. The resulting executables are `/output/test12` and `/output/target/release/test12`. I also compared the Rust binary byte-for-byte against `/workspace/dataset/test12_executable` across the provided examples and additional edge cases, and the outputs matched.
